description: Golden vectors for the normative content_hash of DesignDoc.md S4.1. Each vector carries the written-out preimage as hex, so hashlib.sha256(bytes.fromhex(preimage_hex)).hexdigest() reproduces its digest without importing er.ingest.hashing. The suite asserts oracle == digest == content_hash(row, columns), so a change to the module that changes the digest fails against this file rather than silently rewriting it.

vectors.name: ascii_three_columns
vectors.note: Plain ASCII baseline over the S6 crm column names, in declared order.

vectors.name: extra_unmapped_keys
vectors.note: S4.1 exclusions: ingested_at, ingest_batch_id and std_version are never members of columns, so they cannot reach the preimage. Same digest as ascii_three_columns.

vectors.name: column_order_swapped
vectors.note: Same row, first two columns transposed. Declared order is load-bearing, so the digest differs from ascii_three_columns.

vectors.name: nfd_spelling
vectors.note: Combining acute (NFD). NFC-normalized before hashing, so it shares a digest with nfc_spelling despite different row bytes.

vectors.name: null_value
vectors.note: NULL encodes as the empty string, so this collides with empty_string_value by design (S4.1).

vectors.name: empty_string_value
vectors.note: Empty string in the position null_value leaves NULL. Same digest, by design.

vectors.name: single_column
vectors.note: One-column source: the preimage carries no separator at all.

vectors.name: separator_inside_left_value
vectors.note: A value containing a literal 0x1f is hashed verbatim, never escaped. Its preimage_hex is byte-identical to separator_inside_right_value's -- the 1f at byte offset 7 is indistinguishable from a column boundary, so these two distinct rows share a digest. That ambiguity is a property of the encoding S4.1 pins, and is recorded here rather than worked around.

vectors.name: separator_inside_right_value
vectors.note: The other half of the separator ambiguity documented on separator_inside_left_value.

vectors.name: multibyte_non_latin
vectors.note: Multi-byte CJK and Greek values: the preimage is UTF-8 bytes, not code points.
